comments.author: @mike-jm9rs
comments.text: The Bank will do a short payoff,  they don’t want your house they want your money folks.  They rather sell the loan with other notes in a bundle to another lender than foreclose.  Call them and let them know the situation and let them know your sellers are walking away and will no longer pay their mortgage because they are probably filling for Bankruptcy and I know very well Mr. / Mrs Loan Officer you don’t want that right?  Obviously you would rather have 90% of the loan back than nothing at all,  right?  List it a little bit more than the total of the closing costs, commissions, late fees ect….  are subtracted.  If the bank says no to a short sale,  once the N.O.D. is filled,  they will take offers more times than not.  Get the listing.  Then  price it lower than any of the comps.  Let it be known in the MLS so other agents representing the buyers can let their clients know.  Get an offer and let the bank know you just did them a huge favor by saving them many months of zero money coming in and ending up with a vacant property that will sell for less money anyway,  plus all the money you’ll be losing from the foreclosure, eviction,  ect..  They might say yes or give you a counter offer.  If they don’t then just ride it out,  because they want monthly payments not the house remember.  You and your clients will be better off regardless.  I’m not a Realtor and I don’t know what area or State you’re in so this isn’t professional advice.  Good luck.🍀
